Flora Yukhnovich (b. 1990) is one of the most significant British painters of her generation, known for melding abstraction with the traditions of French Rococo and Italian Baroque. Her work is held in major collections including the Brooklyn Museum, the Hirshhorn Museum, and the National Gallery of Victoria.

All eight pieces in this display were acquired at The Frick Collection during Yukhnovich’s Four Seasons exhibition: four postcards of François Boucher’s The Four Seasons (1755) — part of the Frick’s permanent collection — and four prints of Yukhnovich’s site-specific mural responses to those same works. The Boucher postcards are displayed in ornate oval baroque frames, and the Yukhnovich mural prints in square baroque frames — a deliberate choice that mirrors the Rococo framing style found throughout the Frick’s permanent collection galleries.

Yukhnovich’s Four Seasons installation was the first commission to a contemporary artist at the newly renovated Frick. She described Boucher’s work as “a painter’s dream” — portals that feel like leaping into a painting, as Mary Poppins leaps into a pavement drawing. The installation ran September 2025 – March 2026 in the Cabinet Gallery — the very room where Boucher’s Four Seasons originally hung. Yukhnovich’s murals covered all four walls in response.
